Product Name: EltaMD UV Clear Face Sunscreen SPF 46, Oil Free Sunscreen with Zinc Oxide, Dermatologist Recommended Sunscreen, 1.7 oz Pump
Review Title: good texture but have peel off issues with my NARS foundation
Review: As a regular user of sunscreen products, I was excited to try out this new sunscreen. However, after using it, I encountered some unexpected issues that left me rather disappointed.Prior to applying the sunscreen, I had already completed my skincare routine, using a vitamin C serum and a day cream. When I then applied this sunscreen and proceeded to apply my NARS foundation, I noticed that the foundation started to flake and peel off. This caused me to have to remove the previous skincare products I had applied, which was an inconvenient and undesirable outcome.Interestingly, I have not experienced this issue with other sunscreen brands brought from Japan that I have used in the past. The fact that this sunscreen seemed to interfere with my makeup application/skincare was quite puzzling and frustrating.Overall, while the sunscreen may have provided the necessary UV protection, the incompatibility with my existing skincare and makeup products was a significant drawback. As a consumer, I value products that seamlessly integrate into my routine without causing disruptions. Unfortunately, this sunscreen did not live up to my expectations in this regard.I would caution others who have a similar multi-step skincare and makeup routine to exercise caution when trying this sunscreen, as it may not play nicely with other products. It's always a good idea to do a patch test first to ensure compatibility before committing to using the product regularly.In summary, while this sunscreen may work for some, in my personal experience, it fell short of providing a smooth and hassle-free application experience. I would not recommend this product, especially for those who have a skincare and makeup routine.

Review Title: The rating it deserves depends on your expectations
Review: I noticed that a lot of these reviews are written only after the first few uses of the product so I wanted to have more use out of it before giving my opinion.  Before I get into reviewing I will mention what type of skin I have to give others an idea of what they might expect.Acne has never been a serious problem for me like for some family members of mine.  I rarely have more than 4 zits on my face at a time, but I probably spend about 4 months out of the year with zits on my face. I get ugly brown freckles from the sun (and not the cute kind) so I try to wear sunscreen, but it doesn't seem to matter what type I try and I've tried a LOT- whether they are non-clogging or oil-free or super light or sprays or sticks or lotions or soaps (yes I've even tried the sunscreen soaps) they all seem to make any existing acne on my face worse.  IF I keep a healthy skin regimen I can usually use these sunscreens without them causing acne.. but once I already have it- pfft.  Forget it.  ANYTHING you put over those blemishes aside from acne medication or water makes it worse.  I usually have to wait for the blemishes to dissappear completely before I can start using sunscreen on those areas again, or else they will never dissappear.What I'd really like is a Sunscreen that doesn't just claim to not cause acne but actually CLEARS acne.  Only because in my experience- products that just claim to not cause acne... end up causing it anyway or at least making the ones you already have worse.  Products that aim to TREAT acne (such as certain makeup products that clear up acne while providing coverage) either clear it up or simply prevents it from getting worse.  Such a sunscreen is difficult if not impossible to find.  Probably because the acids used to clear up acne would only eat through any sunscreen product anyway.But when I ordered this I was hoping that maybe they finally got around that problem.  Because I ordered this with the hope that it would either help clear existing acne OR KEEP IT FROM GETTING WORSE.  I personally have not found this to be the case.  It IS the lightest sunscreen I have ever experienced.  5 minutes after putting it on you feel like you just washed your face with water only- It really is THAT good.  So light it actually makes you feel you have nothing on and makes you wonder whether there's any actual protection from the sun at all.  When I first started using this I was so surprised how good and light it felt that I became very excited thinking I have finally found 'the one'!  But now that I've been using it for a few weeks it's become apparent that using this product daily over existing acne gives me the same problem that other products do.  Just makes the acne that's already there worse.  Perhaps not as bad as my other sunscreens- but still worse than with no sunscreen at all.In conclusion-  I think this is a great product if you have oily skin and are prone to acne because I do not think it will CAUSE acne to appear.  However if you already have acne on your face and are hoping this is a sunscreen you can use over your already-acne'd skin without making what's already there worse (ie larger or cystic) , you will probably be dissappointed.  So just like my other 'skin-clearing' sunscreens, I have to shelve this product whenever I have an outbreak.

Review Title: Great first application, not so great reapplication
Review: Hello! Brown girl here (Fenty 370). If you are looking for a sunscreen to start your day this is it, if you are looking for one you can reapply throughout the day, maybe not. Let’s start with the great! This sunscreen is very soothing, almost cooling, easy to spread, doesn’t have a strong smell, and won’t irritate even the most sensitive skin. Massage in for at least 1.5 min and then let it melt into your skin for 10-15 minutes and there will be no white cast (woohoo)! The finish is a little shiny, but not greasy at all and sits extremely well under makeup (provided that you let it sit for that 10-15min). I love it as the last step to my morning face routine.Now for the not so great, reapplication is tough. You can’t massage it in for the entire 1.5 min because the underlying layer of sunscreen will cause it to pill and roll up really bad. Since you can’t do the full massage, the reapplication will leave a slight white cast. Unless you are planning to do a fresh face wash every time, I would recommend a sunscreen stick, gel based, or water based sunscreen for reapplication. This sunscreen is also not sweat proof. You will be sweating milk.

Review Title: Expensive. No white cast, not gritty/tacky/greasy. Leaves skin moisturized.
Review: Update 5/28/18:I initially gave this product 5 stars because it truly is a great product. However I did have to update my review due to the amount of product for the price I paid. This bottle of sunscreen contains 1.7 oz of product. For sunscreen application on the face, it is recommended that you use at least half a teaspoon worth (just for your face alone, not your neck). That half a teaspoon is about 0.083 oz per application. So the bottle can last you 20 applications, not days, applications (since it's recommended you apply every 2 to 3 hours). To pay more than 30 bucks for less than a month's worth of usage seems to be really pricey.//Pleasantly surprised with this sunscreen. I live in Arizona and I know for a fact that I haven't been using as much sunscreen as I should have. The problem was that it was always so tacky, greasy, left a white cast, and irritated my skin. I've been using this sunscreen for at least a week now, and it wasn't irritating to my sensitive skin at all.  It applies easily. It's not watery but has a consistency of a thicker moisturizer. There's an initial cast as you are spreading the sunscreen evenly, but it goes away quite quickly. Sometimes I run into the issue with a gritty feeling left over after I apply sunscreen, I didn't have that issue with this one. It left my skin feeling plump and allowed me to apply my tinted moisturizer/make up after without any issues. I have oily/combo skin and this did not increase my sebum production at all, so that's definitely a plus.The recommended amount of sunscreen to apply to one's face is half a teaspoon (just the face), so this bottle is on the smaller size for what it costs.I had tried this sunscreen on the recommendation of a well-known influencer but had been debating between a more cost-effective (but seemingly just as good alternative). Missha's waterproof Sun Milk is a great contender with this sunscreen, for almost half the price! I'll see how the two compare.

Product Name: EltaMD UV Clear Face Sunscreen SPF 46, Oil Free Sunscreen with Zinc Oxide, Dermatologist Recommended Sunscreen, 1.7 oz Pump
Review: I have actually never left a review on anything before period, but this sunscreen compellingly led me to this moment in my life’s history.The “Add a title” section told me to leave a one line summary of this product and I outdid that by leaving just one word that came to mind… trash.This was the biggest let down of the century. I have heard nothing but fantastic things about Elta MD and I was STOKED to try this product. Until I actually tried it out and hype quickly faded for me.Where do I even begin? Okay first of all, the whole “no cast” spiel is a lie. I get that it’s a mineral based sunscreen and they all leave somewhat of a cast but hear me out on this one folks… you can’t even try to rub this stuff in to eliminate some of the cast before it turns super tacky and starts to pill. I have tried and tried and TRIED to wear this sunscreen without having it looking super streaky on my face or pilling or both. It is incredibly frustrating. I have to wear a mask at my place of work and everyday underneath my mask would be pills of sunscreen. 10/10 looking gross as heck. Whatever remained on my skin never sat well. My skin stayed feeling tacky and just gross. On top of trying to reapply throughout the day and having whatever base layer that may be left gunk up and pill off. I have now come to terms with the fact that this just ain’t the one.The only nice thing I will say about this product is the packaging. The pump is excellent and dispenses an appropriate amount of sunscreen.Personally I will never buy again and have instead found my forever love in the La Roche Posay Anthelios UVMune400. You’re welcome.If I can just save one person from walking around looking like a streaked up Casper the Ghost I’ve done my job.

It's easy to spread if used alone but regardless of what other reviews say, it does leave a white cast if you put on the amount you're supposed to be wearing (a quarter size for your face). I don't wear a ton of moisturizer either so there's no reason for it not to sink into my skin. If I have any type of silicone primer underneath it's impossible to spread evenly because it just slides off my skin. Basically, I can't wear this under makeup or even touch my face. Even after 5+ hours of working inside in AC it still feels like it hasn't settled in. To make the best use of it I'll just mix it with a silicone-free illuminating primer and not wear makeup.It leaves my skin dry/dehydrated especially around my eyes where I see fine lines if I smile. I have to find another spf which is hard because I have fungal acne and other spfs have fragrance, oil, and/or esters but in the meantime I'll finish this bottle.

Product Name: EltaMD UV Clear Face Sunscreen SPF 46, Oil Free Sunscreen with Zinc Oxide, Dermatologist Recommended Sunscreen, 1.7 oz Pump
Review Title: MIGHT (it's still up for debate) be good for your skin but is BAD for the environment.
Review: I was using Elta regularly.  LOVED the smell and while it does go on whitish it clears faster than most, but then I started volunteering with the sea turtle patrol on our local beaches and discovered it has ingredients that are not only possibly bad for humans but known to be bad for the environment, particularly our oceans and waters--and were do we mostly use sunscreen--at the beach!  I've now switched to a mineral based sunscreen that is only zinc (23%) and goes on just as nicely, if not better to avoid adding to our planet's problems.  Some things to consider-*Octinoxate shows up in many sunscreens labeled “natural, but it’s not a natural sunscreen! To make it, they mix sulfuric acid with methanol, a petroleum by-product. This mixture is then heated, until it’s insoluble in water.*It is supposed to simply protect your skin from burns, but instead of staying on your skin, it’s readily absorbed and has been found in human urine, blood and breast milk. It’s absorbed so easily it can take other chemicals with it, so they get into your bloodstream, too.*And it doesn’t just disappear. Like oxybenzone, octinoxate is toxic to coral reefs. According to a study conducted by Environmental Health Perspectives scientists on coral bleaching, octinoxate “caused complete bleaching [of coral] even at very low concentrations.” Many resorts near coral reefs actually require  biodegradable sunscreen. These resorts will not allow specific ingredients in guests’ sunscreen including oxybenzone, octinoxate or parabens, so Elta is out.

Review: This is the only sunscreen I've been able to find that doesn't break me out and it does calm down redness from acne that I have. I love and also don't love it at the same time. Sometimes it can feel a bit heavy on my skin and like it never fully dries down. While other times it dries down great and feels great to apply. Think it depends on how dry my skin is feeling that day. When it's drier this applies nicely. When it is more hydrated this tends to feel heavy, and I use less product because of that.I've tried plenty of Korean sunscreens and a lot of those have ingredients that clog my pores. Some that I've tried are BOJ, this is too heavy, Skin 1004 blue cap one, this is amazing texture and finish-wise but causes me to break out, and roundlab, causes burning when my skin is super dry. I've also tried drmtlgy their zinc sunscreen and that one was horrible with a heavy white cast and heavy feeling to the skin.So, I do use this sunscreen everyday and I have repurchased. Though I wish it would dry down and not leave my face so shiny sometimes. I do use a moisturizer underneath and a toner. I've tried without a moisturizer before and this sunscreen is not hydrating enough for someone with dry/combo sensitive skin. Best solution I've found is to either wait 15mins or more after applying moisturizer and then apply the sunscreen. Or, which isn't ideal, applying a bit less product and kind of doing it in layers.Still looking for a sunscreen I love but this will do in the meantime. If they ever fix it where it dries down with a more matte finish and sinks into the skin better this would be 5 stars.

Product Name: EltaMD UV Clear Face Sunscreen SPF 46, Oil Free Sunscreen with Zinc Oxide, Dermatologist Recommended Sunscreen, 1.7 oz Pump
Review Title: The Best Sunscreen for My Mature, Acne Prone Skin
Review: As a woman past 40 with acne and sensitive skin, I'm constantly searching for sunscreen that doesn't make me break out or irritate.  A couple of years ago, while in the tropics during winter, everyone thought I had a bad sunburn, but no, it was hives all over my chest, neck, and face.  I looked like a swollen lobster, which is not a good look when you are actually eating lobster.I've tried every brand I can find in all different price ranges. Inevitably, I toss the ones that make me break out in hives or are super irritating, and most of the remaining clog my pores or otherwise encourage facial acne, so they end up in a bag for the rest of my family to use. The last time I was at a beach, I just hauled out my failed pricey facial sunscreens, slathered them all over my legs, and wore a gigantic hat.Then my blue-eyed red-headed niece (extremely sensitive to the sun) told me about Elta MD UV Clear Face Sunscreen. Her dermatologist had recommended it because of her acne issues.  I was a bit skeptical because I'd been prescribed all kinds of treatments by my dermatologist, and none of them worked very well, but I've been using the Elta MD all this summer and couldn't be more pleased with the results. I still wear a hat because we all know no sunscreen protects 100%, but most importantly, my skin has actually gotten clearer.It's expensive but worth it if, like me, every other sunscreen makes you break out in rash or pimples. As you can see in the pictures, a small amount goes a long way and is completely sheer with no residue. One pump from the applicator is exactly enough for the face and neck.  Because of the price, I use it only on my face, so my small bottle of Elta MD has lasted for about two months.It's not super moisturizing, but if I apply my moisturizer first and give it time to settle, I can benefit from both. Another great advantage of this lotion is that it can be reapplied without residue building up.  I've used products that get gross after a couple of layers, but this really is very sheer and seems to absorb completely into the skin.There is no added fragrance, so you don't have to worry about weird odors, and Elta MD also makes a tinted sunscreen that I sometimes wear over the UV clear so I can even out my skin tone AND discourage acne.  All around, the best sunscreen I've ever used.

Product Name: EltaMD UV Clear Face Sunscreen SPF 46, Oil Free Sunscreen with Zinc Oxide, Dermatologist Recommended Sunscreen, 1.7 oz Pump
Review: This brand is a good reliable sunscreen.  I first heard about it from an article written by a dermatologist, and I am glad I gave the brand a try.  THIS sunscreen is intended for faces, and I use it along my chest, neck and throat, sometimes my ears.  (I prefer a different sunscreen for my full face.)  This comes out as a completely clear fluid and is easy to spread wherever you want.  It doesn't leave a white cast AT ALL, as it's totally completely see-through.  Absolutely clear.  It does a good job of protecting your skin from sunburn, and I feel confident using it.  The only reason I don't use it for my full face is that it makes my eyes sting a bit when sweating, but in that regard, it's like every other sunscreen I've ever used except for one.  And that "one" is what I use on my face.  This is great for chest, neck, arms and hands - any place you need good reliable sun protection.  Some may find it doesn't sting their eyes - I think mine are just extra-sensitive.  But it's worth using, that's for sure - I never want to be without this, especially in sunny places like California or Florida or Arizona.

Review Title: Had allergic reaction, never buying again
Review: TLDR: I had a severe allergic reaction on my face, never getting this brand again. Several people are having this issue (just look at the “sensitive skin” version of this sunscreen and there’s dozens of people describing my exact experience).I’ve used this product before and had 0 issues, but apparently I’m SEVERELY whatever new ingredient they added to the formula. I put it on my face and arms. Arms were totally fine, face is a different story. My face and neck started to get really itchy after about 2 hours. Even after I washed it off it felt itchy. I had to wash my face three times (with soap) to stop the itching. I was extremely restless afterward, and wasn’t able to get to bed until about 4am (five hours later than when I normally fall asleep). This is SUPER abnormal for me, and I believe it to be directly related to the allergic reaction.When i woke up, my eyes were swollen, my cheeks and forehead were covered in hives, and my skin was a reddish-pink that made me look sunburnt. I was not sunburnt (which is the only thing this product actually did well), and I think the color was because of the hives.I immediately got in the shower, scrubbing my face to make sure there was no sunscreen remaining (making this the fourth wash — with soap — to get this sunscreen off my skin). I ended up needing four Benadryl (over the course of the day, not all at once) and several ointments I already have for my eczema for my skin to calm down. I don’t have issues with acne, but the sheer amount of hives on my face made me look like I had a severe acne problem, THATS how bad it was.Genuinely the WORST experience I’ve ever had with Neutrogena, and a guarantee that I will never buy this brand again, nor will anyone I speak to about this horrible experience. Based on other reviews I’ve seen, I’m not the only one with sensitive skin who is now having issues.TLDR: I had a severe allergic reaction on my face, never getting this brand again. Several people are having this issue (just look at the “sensitive skin” version of this sunscreen and there’s dozens of people describing my exact experience).

Review: I bought this sunscreen as a cheaper and more readily available sunscreen alternative to the Biore Aqua Rich SPF 50 PA+++ sunscreen. I've read good reviews of this sunscreen on beauty forums and on Amazon, but was disappointed when I first used it. The consistency out of the bottle feels like a slightly higher quality sunscreen than the CVS one, but still greasy. I thought the greasiness would go away a few minutes or even 15 minutes after application. Nope. Face is still oily. And sticky. For reference, I am oily around my T-zone and normal everywhere else. In general, I have to blot my entire face 15 minutes after application and put on some powder to look not look like a newly discovered oil field.Since this was a 2-pack and I didn't want to waste it, I wanted to use this sunscreen at least on my body. I thought that maybe the sunscreen didn't play well with my moisturizer. Maybe if I used it on bare skin, it would dry down. Nope. It was still oily AND after a few hours there were white residue, like really tiny coconut shavings, on the folds of my elbow and my wrist.I've never gotten a sunburn while using this product so I guess it does protect from the sun. I just started using actives (A mix of glycolic acid, lactic acid, and niacinimide) and I use this sunscreen to prevent more hyperpigmentation or burns and it does the job fine. Plus, you can actually find these in drugstores if you run out. But, if you decide to use this because you like the claim that it's "dry-touch"? I suggest you go with another sunscreen like the Biore one.

Review Title: "Light feel" leaves powder residue on clothing/swimsuits
Review: I had such high hopes for this sunscreen because all the reviews were so great. Apparently no one who wrote a review wears dark clothing or dark swimwear. This product left white deodorant-like steaks all over one of my navy tank tops, and all over a black one piece swimsuit... Literally the whole suit. I spent the whole day checking myself because people kept pointing them out. It was the discussion of the day. How was it possible I got deodorant all over my body?!? Although it was funny, I couldn't help but be a little embarrassed, and it was the last thing I wanted to be worrying about while enjoying a nice sunny day. Eventually we realized it was this sunscreen, after I reapplied it for the second time. Apparently the "non-greasy feel" this sunscreen DOES have is because it leaves a powder-like residue all over. Um, I'll take a little greasiness over my beloved clothes being messed up. At one point during the day I got so fed up, I used a wet towel to wipe this product off, then borrowed a different sunscreen from a friend. If you're wearing light colored clothing, this product is probably fine and will do the job. But if you're anything like me, and you love black, I would definitely try a different product.

Review Title: Love it for laying out, but use the SPF 30 for daily face/arm/neck etc.
Review: I love the Neutrogena Ultra Sheer Dry-Touch line. It prevents sunburn while still allowing my skin to get some color, it has a non-greasy feel, and it has just a very faint floral scent that is not obnoxiously "beachy."I have been using the SPF 30 formula for a few years and love it because it adds a subtle dewy radiance on my face that works well under makeup, spreads easily, and does not have a white cast.I upgraded to the SPF 45 this summer knowing I'd have access to a pool for a few weeks, and the pro to the SPF 45 formulation is that it does prevent sunburn, does seem to continue working even after getting wet, and also has the same faint floral scent on the SPF30 version. But the cons are that it has a subtle-but-noticable white cast and is thicker and requires more product to spread evenly everywhere. It still dries down/absorbs to be far less greasy than other sunscreens, but it is a little thicker feeling on the body than the SPF30 formula.I usually apply the sunscreen and give it at least 10 minutes to "soak in" before going into the sun, sitting/laying down, letting my hair down, etc. And in that time, the white cast does lessen, and the product does loose some of its initial lotiony oiliness... all in all, though, it feels like a noticeably heavier product than the SPF30.  Which feels great when I'm in a skimpy swimsuit under the hot sun intentionally trying to get a little protective color on my skin for the season, without damaging it, and also not wanting to reapply as frequently if I'm outside for the whole afternoon, but I'll be switching back to the SPF 30 for all other purposes.The SPF30 needs to be re-applied more frequently if you plan to be exposed to the sun for continuous time, but even though it offers less protection, I feel like the formulation is just right in terms of spreadability, absorption time, lack of white cast, and versatility.So 5 stars on SPF45 version in terms of it working as advertised, but 4 stars due to it not being quite as versatile as it's SPF 30 sibling. I feel like I also use much more of the SPF45 than the SPF30 to get the same amount of physical coverage due to it being more viscous.

Review Title: NOT Reef Safe. NOT usable in Hawaii.
Review: I've rated this one star because the title and text say it is "reef friendly" and "safe for use near natural reefs" but ALL of the active ingredients on the back are banned in the state of Hawaii as explicitly NOT reef safe. If you're using this sunscreen anywhere other than a pool, you may be damaging our ecosystems unintentionally. Lakes and rivers may be fine but not in the ocean where our reefs are being killed from the bleaching effects of the chemicals in sunscreens like this. Even if I didn't care about that (which I do) states like Hawaii and many other countries have banned the use of these chemicals, so it feels like an abject LIE to put "reef safe" on the label and heading of the product when it's clearly not!This sunscreen may well work great at protecting skin from sunburns, but I'll never know because I can't use it. I'm also not able to return it because it's considered a flammable item to ship (though Amazon shipped it to me, so that makes no sense), so I am out the money I paid for these items.

Product Name: La Roche-Posay Anthelios Tinted Sunscreen SPF 40+ | Broad Spectrum SPF + Antioxidants | Titanium Dioxide & Zinc Oxide Sunscreen | 4 Flexible Shades With No White Cast | Oil Free & Oxybenzone Free
Review Title: Probably great for medium-dark color skin; not for super pale folk
Review: Loved the texture and as someone who is super sensitive (so sensitive that I have had courses of prednisone/steriods to survive the rashes and reactions to things labeled ‘sensitive skin’ et al…), this one refreshingly did not cause my skin to react BUT… it unfortunately is too dark and orange-y for very light skin like mine.Also, as one who is by profession very picky about color and accuracy (literally, this is what I teach and do as a professor teaching and in my work as a long time professional in the entertainment and creative industries), they over compensated re color on this one. This one (like some of the other new similar ones by these better manufacturers) is too dark AND incorrectly undertoned.For so long, these manufacturers made these tinted mineral sunscreens way too light making it impossible to use for darker skin. Now more than a few have begun to try and fix that but they now have overcompensated AND ended up as well making the same mistake makeup manufacturers of the past made (incorrect undertone). So, as wonderful as this product’s texture and purity is, the color is just not good enough for me and the undertone is too warm (they failed to consider how the skin would look as the product sat on it for awhile and warmed up).Warm undertoned skins may therefore end up looking orange after some hours wearing this and very light colored skin and those who are prone to redness may especially find themselves looking like they just spent a day in the sun.Very disappointing as the texture is fabulous indeed and it truly is one that at least for me did not cauxe my skin to ‘scream’ and complain! I hope they really humble themselves and take some advice from truly expert colorists and makeup artists such as Ms. Brown, Nars, and we who actually have MFAs and Ph.D’s in such stuff. If the manufacturer is reading this, I hope it truly reaches out and accepts help getting this color issue right. It is possible but you need to take advice from the color experts vs. just whoever thinks they’re the expert du jour.

Product Name: La Roche-Posay Anthelios Tinted Sunscreen SPF 40+ | Broad Spectrum SPF + Antioxidants | Titanium Dioxide & Zinc Oxide Sunscreen | 4 Flexible Shades With No White Cast | Oil Free & Oxybenzone Free
Review Title: NOT fully protected if you get the tinted version (no zinc)!
Review: While I love the texture of this product, I found out that you're not fully protected from the longer skin-cancer-causing UVA rays when wearing only Titanium Dioxide; you need Zinc Oxide for that, which is *not* in the tinted version. This is rather irresponsible of La Roche-Posay, in my opinion. Since I specifically want a tinted sunscreen, I won't buy this anymore. If you're interested in what I've found that does work, I tried some out and am currently pretty happy with EltaMD UV Clear Tinted SPF 46, which has a similar consistency to this, plus some anti-aging ingredients, AND offers much more protection because it's formulated with invisible zinc. If I need extra protection that day, I use EltaMD UV Physical, which is thicker. I often follow the EltaMD Clear with IT Cosmetics CC cream (which is also anti-aging and has Zinc - SPF 50!), and I feel much more protected now, with no white cast to boot! You might not see it now because this sunscreen will prevent burning (UVB), but it won't protect you sufficiently from deeper, long-term damage (from UVA1) that contributes to aging and cancer. Sorry, La Roche-Posay - maybe I'll come back if you add Zinc.

I used a few times only but consider it as good for cheek area, and a little irritating for the eye area so I stopped applying closed to eyes. I use it for short walking outside. It has SPF 50 but I am not convinced the sun protection is as high as Avene mIneral sunscreen SPF 50 - which is leaving white on skin so is not acceptable for wearing by adult woman in the city. I have an experience with Bioderma AR SPF 50 sunscreen tinted which always made my face red hot in the evening. Bioderma did not protect so high as declared or was not suitable for rosacea skin although it is reccommeded to use.  The light texture of Bioderma is comparable with Anthelios and that is the reason why it makes me doubt about the protection level.  But : if Anthelios does not lie and protects as declares = no sunburn is possible - then it is a better product than I evaluated.  Right now, I would not use Anthelios minera for whole day stay on the beach - my trust is still limited.  But good for daily use in office job and short time outside.The opened question is - why it is not sold in EUROPE  when it is so good product ?  La Roche-Posay is sold excluding this item.Pavla K.

Review: I generally refuse to pay for fancy-schmancy products (hello, fellow drugstore girlies!) and I resisted the hype. Then I saw an independent test in which a line of photosensitive dots was placed on someone's arm and each dot was covered with a different sunscreen. La Roche-Posay's protection lasted SO MUCH LONGER than my usual drugstore choice! So when Amazon had it on sale for $29, I jumped. And DARN IT, this is a fabulous product. It applies super-smoothly and is very lightweight but offers great coverage. It blends like a dream; I'm over 40, and it doesn't settle in or exaggerate my pores. I use it instead of foundation in the summer, when my makeup is minimal, but you could definitely layer products over it without it pilling. I wish they offered a wider color range for people with darker skin; I really hope that's in the works for the diverse world we live in. But for folks with medium-toned or lighter skin, it's pretty flexible; I had thought it would be too light and too grayish-toned for my olive skin (fyi, I have near-black hair and browns, dark brown eyes), but it melts into my skin well and quickly. When this runs out, though, I still don't know if I can justify repurchasing unless I get another amazing deal; I'll probably just use e.l.f. (which did ok, if not as well, in the testing) and re-apply frequently. Sigh.

Review: I bought this tinted sunscreen for May when we head out for vacation. Obviously, I had to test it and make sure there wouldn't be an issue with the product as a whole. And there were no issues. I shook the product up and per the instructions. Removed the cap and made a thin line on my forehead about 1.5" long. Then, 1 thin line under each eye and a thin line from my left cheek down to my chin and around to my right cheek. It sounds like a lot but the product is just barely thicker than water. I used my fingers lightly to start smearing the product around quickly, covering my jaw and down my neck, up to my temple area, under my eyes, my nose and everywhere it would be visible to others and also to make sure there were no uneven spots or product that got caught in hairs on the sideburn area. Then, I continued with my forehead and hairline. This product is very similar to another product I used that was made by a company that produces hair products that starts with a G. They stopped producing the tinted sunscreen and went to a cream paste, which is greasy and sucks. This product is very thin, dries like powder but needs a few minutes to settle in before it really matches your skin tone. I'm a mix between porcelain and ivory. A little red at times and sometimes look a little colorless. I'm anemic so my skin tone tends to be a little uneven and often very pale. No powder is required with this. You can use it as regular foundation and continue applying your makeup as usual but I found this product to be light as powder, soft on the skin, and not cakey. Perfect really for light day wear and even ladies that are transitioning from their 30's into their 40's and beyond. I found that this product even allowed my natural rosy cheeks to stand out a little and didn't apply anything except a brown mascara to lightly tint my eyelashes and a lightly tinted chapstick. I was ready in less than 10 minutes. It was nice to have my old routine back. If you have blemishes, this would not cover them. I'm going back to buy more. Not only is it great for protecting our skin from the sun but it looks great as makeup.To note: I have very sensitive skin. I'm even on medication for severe psoriasis and it can tend to make your skin sensitive to water temps. *trust me, it sucks* I did not experience any burning, rashes, or have any issues concerning my skin. This product is very gentle.
